change: Segmented Neovim command wheel with release-to-run steering
behavior: Circular mode uses a continuous segmented wheel, with at most eight fixed positions per page and rotated single-line labels kept upright on the lower half. Press/hold the closed button, slide to a sector and release to execute once; hovering never repeats. Returning to the hub, cancelling the touch, or losing control cancels input. Tap opens a persistent menu; outer-ring up/down swipes page and wrap, while center-origin drags steer and never reposition the menu. Groups show a child wheel, center returns to the remembered root page or closes at root. Closed-button quick drags still reposition and persist. The wheel fits inside the terminal without changing the saved resting position. Grid remains six items per page. Arrow/Ctrl shadows remain removed and the idle assistive button retains 50% opacity.
test_notes: The initial UI run passed 13 of 15 cases and exposed Back falling through a non-focusable popup plus native accessibility publication timing. A BackHandler preserves the previous Back behavior, while the native bounds helper allows a frame before retrying. The final full Vim UI suite passed all 15 cases together; three JVM geometry/state checks also passed.
phone_install: Installed release 40 on S22+ RFCT21390SD via USB before finishing the remaining emulator checks, as requested. Installed APK checksum matches; app data preserved; app not launched.
